new_candidates.body:
### Intro

On AMD ROCm (gfx1101, Radeon RX 7800 XT), `mjx.step()` **hangs indefinitely on the first execution** when the model contains an `ACCELEROMETER` sensor.

The JIT compile finishes (`jax.jit(mjx.step)`), then the first call never returns. CPU usage stays around 1.6 % and the load average drops, i.e. the process is blocked on the GPU, not compiling.

Removing only the `ACCELEROMETER` sensors (keeping the other 93 sensors of the model: `jointpos`, `jointvel`, `jointactuatorfrc`, `gyro`, `framequat`, `framepos`, `framelinvel`) makes the same model run at ~13-23 ms/step.

The same model runs fine with the C MuJoCo backend on CPU, and a trivial 1-DoF model with an accelerometer also runs on the same GPU, so the GPU/ROCm stack itself is functional.

The accelerometer is the only sensor type in the model that pulls in `mujoco.mjx._src.smooth.rne_postconstraint`. Skipping that call (workaround below) makes `step()` complete.

Where it hangs: `sensor_acc()` in `mujoco/mjx/_src/sensor.py` calls `smooth.rne_postconstraint(m, d)` whenever the model contains any of `ACCELEROMETER`, `FORCE`, `TORQUE`, `FRAMELINACC`, `FRAMEANGACC`; the accelerometer branch then reads `d._impl.cacc`.

### My setup

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (gfx1101, RDNA3, 16 GB)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel: 7.0.0-38-generic
- ROCm: 7.2.4 (system install, `/opt/rocm`)
- jax: 0.10.0
- jaxlib: 0.10.0
- jax-rocm7-plugin: 0.9.1.post4
- jax-rocm7-pjrt: 0.9.1.post4
- mujoco: 3.17.0
- mujoco-mjx: 3.17.0
- Python: 3.12.3

The plugin/ROCm pairing follows the published compatibility metadata (`jax-rocm7-plugin 0.9.1.post4` -> "Legacy ROCm 7.2.0").

`rocminfo` reports `gfx1101` + `gfx11-generic`. PyTorch (ROCm 7.2 wheel) uses the same card without issues (8.2 TFLOPS measured), and no AMDGPU errors appear in the kernel log during the hang.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

**Observed:** `mjx.step()` blocks forever on the first call (after successful compilation). Effectively a GPU-side deadlock: CPU ~1.6 %, no kernel-log errors.

**Expected:** `mjx.step()` completes and produces accelerometer readings (or at least does not hang) on ROCm for models containing accelerometer sensors.

## Evidence from bisecting the Unitree G1 29-DoF model

Model: `unitree_mujoco/unitree_robots/g1/scene_29dof.xml` (29 actuators, nq=36, nv=35). Mesh collision geoms were replaced by primitives (required by MJX per doc note [3]); visual meshes kept.

| Model variant | sensors | result |
|---|---|---|
| full model | 95 | hang (timeout 400 s) |
| no meshes | 95 | hang |
| reduced contact set (13 collidable geoms) | 95 | hang |
| all sensors removed | 0 | **OK, 13.7 ms/step** |
| only `jointpos` (29) | 29 | OK |
| only `jointvel` (29) | 29 | OK |
| only `jointactuatorfrc` (29) | 29 | OK |
| only `gyro` (2) | 2 | OK |
| only `framequat` (2) | 2 | OK |
| only `framepos` (1) | 1 | OK |
| only `framelinvel` (1) | 1 | OK |
| **only `accelerometer` (2)** | 2 | **hang** |
| everything except accelerometers | 93 | OK |

Control experiments:
- MJX `test_data/humanoid/humanoid.xml` (21 actuators): OK, 2-4 ms/step.
- A single sphere on a plane with a free joint: OK, ~1.1 ms/step.
- `iterations` in {1, 5, 20, 100}: no effect.
- `--xla_gpu_enable_cublaslt=false`, `--xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false`, `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`, `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=`: no effect.
- C MuJoCo on CPU with the same file: stable.

## Workaround used locally

Patch `sensor.py` so `ACCELEROMETER` neither triggers `rne_postconstraint` nor reads `cacc` (the sensor entry stays in the model, `sensordata` left at 0; the training code computes gravity direction from the base quaternion):

```python
# 1) do not trigger rne_postconstraint for accelerometers only
if sensor_types & {
    int(SensorType.FORCE),
    int(SensorType.TORQUE),
    int(SensorType.FRAMELINACC),
    int(SensorType.FRAMEANGACC),
}:
    d = smooth.rne_postconstraint(m, d)

# 2) accelerometer branch
elif sensor_type == SensorType.ACCELEROMETER:
    sensor = jp.zeros((int(idx.sum()), 3), dtype=jp.float32)
    adr = (adr[:, None] + np.arange(3)[None]).reshape(-1)
```

With the patch the full 95-sensor G1 model steps at ~19-23 ms/world and batches to ~5.6k world-steps/s at 256 worlds.

## Related
- #3716 (MJX accelerometer reads `cacc` directly, reports `-gravity` on static/mocap bodies)
- PR #3717 (zero acceleration sensors on static and mocap bodies)
- mujoco_warp#1804 (same accelerometer issue in the Warp backend)
- ROCm/jax#745 (gfx1100/ROCm 7.2 JAX issues, fixed by jax 0.10.0 + plugin 0.9.1.post4 — the combination used here)

### Steps for reproduction

1. Save the XML below as `accel.xml`.
2. Run the Python snippet on a ROCm gfx1101 machine (jax 0.10.0 / plugin 0.9.1.post4 / mjx 3.17.0).
3. Observe that `step()` never returns (hangs on first execution).

```xml
<mujoco>
  <option timestep="0.002"/>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1"/>
    <body name="base" pos="0 0 0.8">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="capsule" size="0.05 0.2"/>
      <site name="imu" size="0.01"/>
      <body name="link" pos="0 0 -0.25">
        <joint name="j0" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"/>
        <geom type="capsule" size="0.03 0.15" pos="0 0 -0.15"/>
        <site name="imu2" size="0.01"/>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
  <actuator>
    <motor joint="j0" ctrlrange="-5 5"/>
  </actuator>
  <sensor>
    <gyro site="imu"/>
    <accelerometer site="imu"/>
    <accelerometer site="imu2"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>
```

```python
import jax, mujoco, mujoco.mjx as mjx

m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path("accel.xml")
print(f"nu={m.nu} nq={m.nq} nv={m.nv} nsensor={m.nsensor}")
mx = mjx.put_model(m)
d = mjx.make_data(m)
step = jax.jit(mjx.step)

print(jax.devices())     # [RocmDevice(id=0)]
d = step(mx, d)          # <-- hangs here
jax.block_until_ready(d.qpos)
print(float(d.qpos[2]))
```

The same XML compiles and runs with the stock MJX on CPU (`nu=1 nq=8 nv=7 nsensor=3`, `sensordata` length 9), so the model itself is valid.

### Minimal model for reproduction

If you encountered the issue in a complex model, please simplify it as much as possible (while still reproducing the issue).

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML

<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <light pos="0 0 1"/>
    <geom type="sphere" size="1" rgba="1 0 0 1"/>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>

```
</details>


### Code required for reproduction

[repro_accel_hang.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34181821/repro_accel_hang.py)

[repro_accel_hang.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34181833/repro_accel_hang.py)

```python
import mujoco
import mediapy as media
model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml)
data = mujoco.MjData(model)

with mujoco.Renderer(model) as renderer:
  mujoco.mj_forward(model, data)
  renderer.update_scene(data)

  media.show_image(renderer.render())
```
